items.headline: Draw shirt backs before filming to fix flat-photo gaps.
items.background: E-commerce and tutorial creators often work with product photography that only captures one angle, leaving gaps when demonstrating features that reference physical or spatial attributes of an item. This post describes a practical pre-production workaround developed during tutorial recording.
keyFindings: Flat lay T-shirt photos lack back and side views, creating continuity problems in video tutorials
The author's solution is to sketch or illustrate missing angles before recording begins, not during editing
This pre-production step prevents mid-recording interruptions caused by missing visual assets
items.implications: Relevant for anyone producing instructional content around physical products with incomplete photography. Building a visual asset checklist before recording — not after — saves significant rework time.

items.headline: How parenthood drove one designer to rethink voice UI.
items.background: Voice interfaces have existed for years on mobile, but desktop app voice mode remains underdesigned and underexplored. Most design guidance assumes a touch or keyboard context, leaving voice interaction patterns for desktop largely undocumented.
keyFindings: The author began using voice mode out of necessity as a parent with limited hands-free time, not by choice
Desktop voice UI requires different affordances than mobile — persistent visibility of activation state matters more on larger screens
Key design challenges include discoverability of voice mode and managing interruption states in multi-window environments
items.implications: If you're designing desktop productivity tools, voice interaction is no longer a fringe case — caregivers, accessibility users, and power users are reaching for it. Consider persistent status indicators and graceful interruption handling as baseline requirements.

items.headline: Build search demand before your product launches, not after.
items.background: Most marketing and SEO efforts begin at or after product launch, meaning brands spend the early weeks of a release with no existing search visibility or indexed content. This piece argues that search demand can and should be seeded during pre-launch.
keyFindings: Waiting until launch day to start SEO means Google has no indexed content to surface when demand spikes
Pre-launch content strategies — including problem-focused landing pages and informational blog content — can begin building domain authority months earlier
Search interest can be stimulated before a product exists by targeting adjacent problem queries rather than product-name queries
items.implications: For product and growth teams: coordinate with SEO and content earlier in the roadmap, not at the go-to-market phase. Pre-launch landing pages targeting problem-space queries are a low-cost way to validate interest and build indexing simultaneously.

items.headline: 63 clicks, zero conversions: what a failed landing page taught about validation.
items.background: Fake door and landing page tests are a common lean validation method, but many practitioners treat ad click-through as sufficient proof of demand. This post is a first-person account of a 2020 test that exposed a gap between traffic and actual intent.
keyFindings: 63 paid ad clicks to a landing page produced zero conversions, despite the ads themselves performing well by standard metrics
The disconnect was between the ad promise and the landing page's ability to communicate the product's value clearly enough to prompt action
The author concludes that click-through rate alone is not a reliable signal of product-market fit — conversion on the page is the real test
items.implications: When running pre-build validation tests, clicks are a weak signal. Design your landing page to require a meaningful commitment — email signup, waitlist join, or simulated purchase — before treating the data as validation. Optimize both the ad and the page as a system.

items.headline: Sterling Bank and Google offer fully funded tech certifications for women.
items.background: Access to formal tech credentials remains uneven across gender and geography, particularly in emerging markets. Fully funded programs targeting underrepresented groups are a recurring mechanism to address this gap.
keyFindings: The program is 100% fully funded for women applicants
It is associated with Google Career Certificates, which cover job-ready skills in IT, UX, data, and project management
The program targets applicants in the Global South with a 2027 enrollment cycle
items.implications: If you mentor early-career women in tech or UX in eligible regions, this is a concrete resource to share. Google Career Certificates have documented employer recognition and are a legitimate pathway into UX research and product roles.

items.headline: IIT Delhi vs IIT Bombay design programs compared.
items.background: India's IIT institutions offer design programs that are increasingly competitive, but prospective students often lack a clear side-by-side comparison of curriculum focus, entry requirements, and career outcomes between campuses.
keyFindings: IIT Delhi and IIT Bombay both offer design programs but differ in curriculum structure and specialization tracks
The comparison is published by an education marketing platform, so editorial independence should be considered
No specific outcome data — placement rates, alumni roles — is cited in the available snippet
items.implications: Useful context if you're advising students on design education pathways in India, but verify details directly with institutions given the source's commercial nature.
